agendas.flag: The Proclamation never fired in 29 arms (no formation reached), so the formables road stays unjudged even where the licence, the Revanche promotions and the tether lines all read well.

flags: On every commanded seed the titled count stalls at 34–36 after the turn-10 settlement and the ledger reads 'provinces 30 (+0)' for thirty quiet turns, while on the PRESS fixture six mornings of the climactic sitting are led by 'Garrison at Lisbon reinforced: 14,000 -> 16,000' — a human should check whether a played France can reach 45 at all and whether the sitting gives the player anything to do.

PRESS.md L179 'THE RECORD — battles 0 (0 won, 0 lost) · men lost 0, inflicted 0 · provinces taken 11, lost 0' on the staged Imperial Peace — check whether the record is blind to the fixture's history or the fixture starts with an empty record.

PRESS.md:179 closes the staged Imperial Peace on a RECORD of 0 battles, 0 men lost and 0 peaces signed — a human should check whether an ending with nothing behind it should read as THE ASCENDANT EMPIRE, and whether the CMD arms' 30-turn plateau at 34–36 titled is the road a player actually walks.

CMD-H accepts Sweden's defensive-alliance offer three times and each is refused at ratification ('Sweden's terms could not be ratified: Relations with France are insufficient for DEFENSIVE_ALLIANCE') — the AI offers what it cannot sign; and on nearly every multi-envoy morning the first answer bounces ('another matter has arrived since … Your earlier answer was not delivered') and must be given twice.

On all three PROP arms every 'propose peace with Austria/Britain' for ten turns dies at 'I cannot deliver this, Sire — Making peace with Austria while allied with Bavaria (who is…' (PROP-H.md L10, L83, L137); peace only ever arrives via the AI's own settlement offer — check whether the ally-paradox wall is meant to shut the player's peace road entirely.

The 'Sire, another matter has arrived since … Your earlier answer was not delivered' re-prompt fires on nearly every multi-envoy turn on every arm (e.g. FLAG.md:180, OP.md:354–359 with five dialogues raised on one turn) — a human should check whether it costs the player a wasted answer or a diplomatic point.

HOLD's natural phrasings are shrugged 16 times in 20 — 'How much gold do we have right now, and what do we actually clear per turn…' gets 'I cannot answer that from the dispatches' while TYPED's terse 'what's my income' is answered to the gold; a human should type a few long sentences on turn 1.

HOLD.md L73: inside the '## Turn 2' block the reply to `end turn` reads '✓ Turn 3 ended. (Warning: 4 actions unused) Turn 4 begins!' — a turn appears to have been skipped or the counter is off by one after the load.

HOLD.md:10 shrugs at 'Who is Deroy, and is he on our side or against us?' while Deroy is Bavaria's marshal fighting beside France from turn 1 (FLAG.md:46) — a human should check whether the desk should know an ally's commander.

At peace the chest runs to 91,878 on CMD-H by turn 40 ('LEDGER treasury 91878 · net +2545 · threat 3') with the open-levy nag as the only spending prompt — partly the driver's passivity, but a human should check whether a peaceful France has anything worth buying.

VOLTE.md L887 'LEDGER treasury 89817 · net +2283 · threat 0' sits beside L872 'the levy has stood open 30 turns' — at a long peace the hoard has no sink and the levy nag never stands down; check whether both are intended.
CMD-A.md:749 ends turn 40 at treasury 86,368, net +2,409, threat 0 — a human should check whether a 30-turn peacetime hoard with no sink but the open levy is the intended feel of a won war.

DESC.md's 'land Oudinot in Munster with 5,000 men' is answered about a different marshal ('The transports lift 15,000 men; Lannes commands 18,000 — 3,000 too many') four turns running, and both naval arms close with 'every expedition line in the script was refused' — the descent was never reachable on these arms.

DESC.md L267: `land Oudinot in Munster with 5,000 men` is answered 'The transports lift 15,000 men; Lannes commands 18,000 — 3,000 too many' — Oudinot was never commissioned on that arm (L95) and the reply re-addressed Lannes without saying so.

DESC.md:267 answers an order for Oudinot ('land Oudinot in Munster with 5,000 men') with Lannes's numbers ('Lannes commands 18,000 — 3,000 too many') and the whole descent arm's expedition lines were refused — the expedition itself was never played on any arm.

After the turn-10 general peace all three commanded seeds run thirty turns of 'enemy phase: 1 actions, 0 attacks' with the alarm decaying to 0 and no court moving against France; the armed peace never arrives, so the post-peace board reads as a finished game that keeps running.

Every commanded arm (CMD-H, CMD-A, CMD-M, VOLTE, CMDR-H) reaches a first peace by turn ~10 and then plays 25–30 turns of 'enemy phase: nothing visible' with threat falling to 0 and the marshals cycling fortify/drill — the world stops pushing back after the first peace.

REACH-AAR.md:857–858 — from turn 18 to turn 40 every turn is a bare 'end turn' with '(Warning: 4 actions unused)' and '0 attacks' while threat decays 31 → 0; a human should check whether a France at peace has anything to do or anyone to fear.

Every enemy-phase summary prints raw keys ('ArchdukeCharles's forces press forward aggressively') while the battle lines beneath humanise the same man, and the opening exchanges run 8:1 to 40:1 (SEA.md: 'Murat (lost 602, own corps) vs Mack (lost 26060)') — a human should sanity-check the muster arithmetic against the results.

CMD-ULM.md L16 renders the enemy-phase summary with raw keys ('ArchdukeCharles attacks with overwhelming force…') while the battle row beneath it (L17) humanizes 'Archduke Charles' — the same event in two registers on one screen.

FLD.md:123 scouts Vienna's garrison at 25,000 ('it must be assaulted — a march halts before it'), yet FLD.md:153–156 'Ney, attack Vienna' resolves as a field battle against Mack and Vienna is captured with no assault line — a human should check whether the garrison was silently bypassed.

DL.md: 'Murat, come to Ney's support' draws the objection 'Murat: You ask me to bleed for Bernadotte? That man would see me destroyed!' — the objection names a marshal the order did not; and the reward-arrears line runs 34 mornings on CMD-H with no visible consequence.

The shadow_command acknowledgement is one template for every marshal — 'X straightens. "You will not regret it, Sire."' for Davout (PROP-A.md L155), Ney (PROP-M.md L140), Murat (SHUT-H.md L287), Massena (FLAG.md L231) — and the arrears dispatch ('Marshal Lannes's claim is N turns in arrears … a question of the army') leads 30+ consecutive turns on REACH-AAR with no visible consequence.

CMD-A.md:138 '- DISPATCH: Sire — Ney, crowned four turns ago, has been beaten in the field.' (also CMD-ULM.md:205, REACH-GEVB.md:191) shows a crown won and lost on the arms — a human should reconcile this with the checklist's C4 note that no crown moved.

Under refusal the satellites bleed 3 loyalty a turn for fifteen turns with no dispatch line until 'Sire — Switzerland is on the verge of rebellion!' (CMDR-H, rebellion at turn 22); the ledger figure is the only earlier warning.

CMD-ULM.md: Holland drifts 84 → 7 over turns 9–31 with only 'diplomatic_vassal_courting' DIPLO rows and no dispatch naming a remedy until 'Holland is on the verge of rebellion!' (L714) — the loyalty-under-40 counsel the checklist marks MISSING is visible in play.

REACH-GEVB.md:9 'vassalize Bavaria' on turn 1 makes an allied minor a Satellite at loyalty 60 with no battle and no price shown (Hesse and Saxony likewise at REACH-GEVB.md:102–103, both lost within eight turns) — a human should check whether free turn-1 vassalization of an ally is intended.

OP's turn-10 end turn stacks five blocking dialogues (armistice, settlement offer, settlement confirm, pair-substitute confirm, and a disabled proposal confirm left standing) — a human should see how that stack reads in the client.

On every arm a queued second envoy bounces the first answer ('Your earlier answer was not delivered') and the driver must answer twice (SEA.md L288–L295; VERDICT.md L333–L340 ×10) — in the client this is two modals for one decision; the human pass should watch the stacking.
OP.md:354–359 raise five diplomatic dialogues on one turn and leave the last standing disabled — a human should check what a player at the keyboard sees when that stack lands.

HOLD.md: 'Murat, hunt Mack down before he can slip away.' → "Cannot find 'Mack Down' to pursue." — the natural sentences a new player types are refused or, worse, executed on a misread ('In Support Of Ney' became a destination); the terse grammar in TYPED.md works well.

HOLD.md L56 `Murat, hunt Mack down before he can slip away.` → '✗ Cannot find 'Mack Down' to pursue.' and L71 `We're short of guns - raise some artillery at Paris.` → 'There is no 'We're' in the order of battle' — the addressee reader takes the sentence's first word as a name; both are prose a new player would type.

SHUT-M.md:106 — one order after Mack's corps was annihilated (SHUT-M.md:104), 'Davout, attack Mack' was answered 'Your words named no foe our maps know, Sire — Davout marches on Archduke John at Bohemia, the nearest in sight' and a battle followed; a human should check whether an order naming a dead foe should act rather than ask.

On all four peaceful 40-turn arms the morning dispatch alternates the same two nags (Lannes's arrears, the open levy) for thirty consecutive turns; the voice is excellent when something happens and inert when nothing does.

The Congress sitting turns on PRESS.md lead with 'Garrison at Lisbon reinforced: 12,000 -> 14,000' (L65, L80, L96) while the Congress itself sits — and CMD-H.md L203 'Paget has crossed into Berry' leads the turn Massena captured Moravia; the lead picker under-weights the player's own events and the standing arcs.

The arrears sentence leads the dispatch with only its number changing on 20+ consecutive mornings on REACH-AAR, VOLTE and CMD-H — a human should check whether a standing grievance should keep the headline once it has been said.
The campaign log is dominated by AI-AI refusal roll-ups ('26 approaches from Prussia, Bavaria and Austria are rebuffed (open borders agreement)') on almost every turn — alive, but noisy.

The 'ai_ai_proposal_refused' rows read '26 approaches rebuffed, chiefly from Bavaria and Prussia (open borders agreement)' on nearly every turn of every arm (SEA.md L68, DESC.md L58, ADV.md L51) — check whether the AI's open-borders asks should cool down after a refusal; CMD-A.md L146 also logs 'Britain sponsors Bavaria against France' while Bavaria is France's ally.

Courts repeatedly harden 'prepared now to go as far as war' (e.g. CMD-ULM.md:825 Russia over Arbiter of Europe) yet no AI court opens a war of its own on any of the 29 arms — a human should check whether the tether line promises something the board never delivers.
Sardinia's court 'hardens'/'eases' over The House of Savoy Restored every few turns on OP and FLD — the oscillation reads as noise; no formable nation was sighted on any played arm.

The COURTS lines alternate 'hardens' and 'eases' for the same court every few turns (PROP-A.md L115 Sardinia eases, L177 hardens, L196 eases) and the phrase 'X is now the length of its tether' is never explained on the surface — a human should check whether the tether metaphor reads to a new player.
The Proclamation never fired in 29 arms (no formation reached), so the formables road stays unjudged even where the licence, the Revanche promotions and the tether lines all read well.
